root.name: Benoni Defense: Franco-Sicilian Hybrid
root.moves: 1. d4 e6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 exd5 4. cxd5 d6 5. Nc3 g6 6. e4 Bg7 7. Nf3 Ne7

overview: The Franco-Sicilian move order reaches a Modern Benoni-style structure after 3.d5 exd5 4.cxd5 d6 and the fianchetto on g7. White takes the centre with e4 and Nf3, and Black develops with ...Ne7 and prepares ...O-O and ...b5 or ...f5. White has space; Black counterattacks on the queenside and the e-file.

white_ideas.idea: Build the e4-d5 centre and play Be2, O-O
Attack with e5 or play for a kingside space advantage

black_ideas.idea: Use the half-open e-file and g7 bishop
Break with ...f5 or ...b5 at the right moment

typical_structures.structure: Benoni pawn structure: White d5/e4 against Black c5/d6

character.notes: The Benoni structure gives unbalanced positions with chances for both sides.

soundness.notes: Sound; it is a Benoni by transposition.

structure.notes: The d5/c5 centre is locked or semi-locked, with play on the wings.

approach.notes: A transposition into a standard Benoni set-up.

level.notes: Plans must be understood but the move order is easier than the Modern Benoni.
